title: Paloma and the Ember
premise: Yara Underhill has spent her life in Emberfall Valley, where the wards keep magic out and her work as royal food-taster keeps poison in — until the wards collapse on the night every star vanishes, and a dying dragon's ember falls into her hands. The ember is the last living spark of dragon-fire, and it is bound to King Aldric, whose crown has been slowly replaced by a parasite of old magic called the Hollow Regent. Guided by Sef, a disgraced court mage who once loved her, Yara must carry the ember through a starless kingdom to unbind the king before the fire gutters out and the Regent's memory-eating hunger consumes everything. She succeeds at the cost of her own memories of the valley, choosing love against duty one final time: she gives the ember what it needs to reignite the sky, and wakes remembering nothing but a warmth in her chest and a stranger named Sef who refuses to let her forget again.
about_author: Theo Whitlock is the pen name of a former line cook who swears the best fantasy is written by people who have worked a kitchen during a dinner rush. They live somewhere rainy with two cats and an unreasonable number of unfinished manuscripts.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A day in Emberfall Valley: tasting the king's distant tribute dishes, trading barbs with Sef, the exiled mage who delivers them, and hinting that the wards hum strangely tonight. The emotional beat is quiet contentment laced with dread — Yara loves a life she suspects cannot last.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At midnight the wards shatter like glass and every star goes out at once; a burning ember crashes into the palace kitchens, searing itself to Yara's palm. Sef arrives bloodied, saying the border fell from the inside. The beat is terror and awe as her small world ends in firelight.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Brought before King Aldric, Sef recognizes the Hollow Regent coiled beneath the crown, feeding on the king's memories. Aldric, lucid for one moment, begs Sef to find the ember before he forgets his own name. The beat is horror tempered by loyalty to a fading friend.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Gone Dim
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yara and Sef flee the capital as the Regent's hunters — knights whose faces are smooth as eggs — sweep the city. Yara learns the ember answers her heartbeat, not Sef's spells. The beat is reluctant partnership hardening into trust on the road north.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They shelter in a town where the Regent's hunger has already passed: people remember how to work but not why, or whom they love. Yara realizes the ember could restore them but might gutter out entirely. The beat is the first true test of duty versus mercy.

chapters.title: Ashes of the First Dragon
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. In the caldera ruins, a blind elder dragon named Vessk reveals the truth: the Regent was once the dragons' keeper, betrayed, and the ember is its stolen heart. Unbinding the king means giving the Regent back what it lost. The beat is moral vertigo — the monster has a grievance.

chapters.title: The Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hunters corner them; Yara discovers her years of building poison-immunity made her body a vessel the ember chose deliberately — she can hold it whole, but it will drink her memories as fuel. Sef begs her to refuse. The beat is love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Storming the Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With Vessk's last strength, they assault the starless citadel. Sef duels the Regent's high knight while Yara reaches the throne room, where Aldric barely remembers his own daughter's face. The beat is desperate momentum, losses mounting, no way back.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the throne dais, Yara offers the ember not as a weapon but as a returned heart; the Regent falters between vengeance and grief. She lets it take her memories of the valley as kindling to relight it. The beat is sacrifice rendered intimate — she chooses forgetting so others may remember.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, closing on Yara. Stars return; Aldric, freed, kneels to a girl who doesn't know why. Yara wakes in the rebuilt valley kitchen, a warmth in her chest and no past — until Sef sits across the table and begins telling her their story, determined to give her every memory back. The beat is bittersweet hope: love that starts over and refuses to end.
